about: About these leads

Leaflegal sends licensing enquiries from businesses and individuals in England and Wales who want to pay a solicitor to help with a licence. They come from pubs, bars, restaurants, late night venues, shops selling alcohol, event organisers, taxi and private hire drivers and operators. Each enquiry goes to one firm only. It is never sent to several firms at once and it is never resold after delivery.

Licensing clients usually have something real at stake. A new venue cannot open without the right licence, a review could put an established business at risk, and a driver whose licence is suspended may lose their income overnight. Many have a hearing date, an opening date or a deadline from the council, and they want representation they can rely on.

Enquiries come from operators, licence holders and applicants, not from residents or other members of the public who want to object to a licence. That means every lead is a potential client who needs help with their own licence or business.

Our campaigns run on search, social media and helpful content aimed at licensees, venue owners and drivers. Each person answers a short set of questions about the type of licence, what they need, any hearing or opening date, the council area and the name of the business. When an enquiry matches your criteria, we check it and send it to you straight away.

Many licensees do not know where to start when something goes wrong. Some assume they can deal with a review alone and only look for help once the paperwork arrives. Others are not sure whether they need a licensing specialist or a general solicitor. Our questions steer them to a firm that does licensing work, so they reach you with a clear idea of what they need help with, even if they do not yet know the process.

Licensing work is often relationship work. A venue owner who is well represented at a review hearing may come back for variations, transfers and new sites for years. Multi site operators and drivers' networks also talk to each other. An exclusive introduction gives you a fair chance to build that relationship from the first call.

Leaflegal is not a law firm and does not give legal advice. We do not tell a client whether their application will be granted, how a committee is likely to decide or what conditions they should offer. We introduce them to one firm that handles licensing, and the advice comes from you.
Who enquires

Licensing enquiries cover a broad mix of businesses and individuals. You choose the licence types and matter types you want, so a firm that focuses on premises work does not have to take taxi enquiries unless it wants them.

about.h3: Where they are in the process

about: Some clients are planning a new venue months ahead and want help with the application and the plans. Others have received notice of a review, a letter from the police or a complaint from environmental health and want representation quickly. Drivers often enquire after a council has suspended or refused to renew their licence. Each lead tells you whether there is a hearing or opening date, so you can see the urgency before you call.

Licensing clients want someone who knows how their council and its committee work, who can deal with the police and other responsible authorities, and who can give a clear idea of cost. A business facing a review also wants reassurance that its side of the story will be put properly. A calm, practical first conversation goes a long way.

Multi site operators sometimes enquire about one venue while planning changes across several. The description in the client's own words often mentions this, and it can be worth asking about on the first call.
Lead details
Every licensing lead is the full record of what the client told us. The questions are short, but they give you what you need to judge urgency and decide who in your team should call.

about: Licensing is run by local authorities, and each one has its own statement of licensing policy, its own committee practices and, in some places, special policies for particular areas. Knowing the council before you call lets you speak to the client about what you know of that authority, in general terms, and decide whether the matter fits your coverage.

Taxi and private hire licensing is also run by councils, and each sets its own policies on matters such as driver standards and vehicle requirements. For drivers and operators, the council area tells you which policy and which appeal route are likely to be relevant.

Having the business name lets you run conflict checks before the first call and look at publicly available information, such as the existing licence on the council's register. That means you can open the conversation already understanding something about the premises.

Every client confirms they want paid help with their own licence or business in England and Wales, and their mobile number and email address are checked. Objectors and people with matters outside our scope are filtered out. Each client ticks one box to confirm they understand Leaflegal is an introduction service and a separate box to agree to one firm contacting them by phone, email or text. We record the wording and the time and send it with the lead. Leads arrive as soon as they are checked, by email, to a shared inbox or into your CRM or case management system.
Working the lead
Licensing enquiries reward firms that respond quickly and show they understand how licensing works on the ground.

A business that has received notice of a review, or a driver whose licence has been suspended, will usually instruct the first firm that gives them confidence. Calling soon after a lead arrives, at the time they asked for, matters. Set up alerts so the right fee earner sees licensing leads straight away.

about.h3: Start with the date and the council

about: The lead tells you the licence type, the matter type, any hearing or opening date and the council. Opening with those shows the client you have read their enquiry and lets you deal first with anything urgent, such as a deadline for evidence or a hearing in a few days.

Many licensing clients want a fixed fee for an application or a clear estimate for preparing for and attending a hearing. Being clear about what is included, such as plans, liaison with responsible authorities and attendance at the hearing, helps the client decide on the call.

After the call, a short email confirming the fee, the next step and the information you need, such as plans, the existing licence or any letters from the council or police, keeps things moving. Clients facing a hearing in particular value a clear list of what happens next and when.

A venue owner may have other sites, plans to extend hours or staff who need personal licences. A driver may know other drivers in the same position. Asking about the wider picture, without pushing, can open the door to further work.

The client agreed to be contacted after making an enquiry through Leaflegal. Mention that when you call, and cover any referral arrangement in your client care letter as the SRA Code of Conduct requires.
Let us know which leads instruct and which do not. If reviews convert well for you but personal licence enquiries do not, we can change your matching to send you more of the work you want.
Compliance
Licensing work brings clients into contact with councils, the police and the courts. Your professional duties apply in full, and Leaflegal is set up to support them.

Leaflegal is an introducer. Under the SRA Code of Conduct, you must make sure clients are told in writing about any financial arrangement with an introducer, and that it does not affect your independence or advice. Our consent wording tells every client we are paid by the firms we introduce them to, and we send that wording with each lead.

Licensing enquiries go to SRA regulated firms and CILEx regulated practices authorised for the work, including rights of audience where you appear on appeal in the magistrates' court. You remain responsible for your own conflict checks, which can matter where you already act for a competing venue, a council or a responsible authority in the same area.

We only send enquiries from licence holders, applicants, operators and drivers. We do not send enquiries from residents or groups who want to object to a licence, so you will not receive a lead that conflicts with acting for the licensed trade.

Some licensing enquiries, especially reviews and taxi matters, can involve allegations of offences or criminal records, which UK data protection law treats as criminal offence data. We keep our questions to the minimum needed for first contact and never pass matter details to advertising platforms. Leaflegal, a trading name of Vertical Brands Ltd, is the controller for data collected on our forms. Once a lead is delivered, you are controller of your copy.
Read more about referral rules and introducers.
Pricing

You pay for each licensing lead we deliver, at a price agreed with you before you start. There is no retainer for advertising and no shared or recycled data, so you can measure each lead against the instructions and fees it produces.

Price depends on the licence types, matter types and areas you choose. A premises licence review or a new late night venue application is usually worth more to a firm than a personal licence enquiry, and wide coverage produces more matches than a single council area. We talk this through on a call and put a proposal together.

The minimum is 10 leads a month. Above that, you tell us how many your team can handle and we match to that number. You can set a monthly cap, change it and pause at any time, for example during a busy run of hearings or when a key fee earner is away.

Before your first lead, we agree a written partner agreement covering pricing, billing, volumes, delivery and the rules on invalid leads. If a lead has wrong contact details or falls outside your agreed criteria, tell us within the review period in your agreement and we will deal with it as the agreement says.

Onboarding starts with a 30 minute call with our team. We talk about the licensing work you handle, the councils you cover and your volume, and we show you a sample lead before you commit. You can apply to become a partner firm to book the call.
faqs: The leads
What is a licensing lead from Leaflegal?

It is an enquiry from a business or individual in England and Wales who wants to pay a solicitor to help with a licence. They have told us the licence type, whether it is a new application, a variation, a transfer or a review, any hearing or opening date, the council area and the business name, confirmed their contact details and agreed to be contacted by one firm.
Are licensing leads exclusive?

Yes. Each enquiry goes to one firm only and is never resold. We do not send the same venue or driver to several firms at once. That gives you the chance to have a proper first conversation, which matters in licensing because many clients come back for further work once they trust a firm.
Do you send enquiries from objectors?

No. Our licensing enquiries come from licence holders, applicants, operators and drivers who want help with their own licence or business. We do not send enquiries from residents or groups who want to object to a licence. That keeps the leads consistent with acting for the licensed trade and avoids an obvious source of conflict.
Which licence types can I receive?

You can choose premises licence work, personal licences, and taxi and private hire licensing, and within those you can choose new applications, variations, transfers and changes of designated premises supervisor, and reviews and hearings. You can take all of them or only the kinds of work your team wants, and change your choice later.
Will I know if there is a hearing date?

Yes. Each lead includes any hearing date or planned opening date the client knows about. A venue facing a review next week and a business planning to open in six months need very different first calls, and the lead tells you which you are dealing with before you pick up the phone.
Why do you include the business name?

The business name lets you run conflict checks before you call and look at publicly available information, such as the existing licence on the council's register. That way you can open the conversation already knowing something about the premises, which helps show the client you have taken their enquiry seriously.
Do you send taxi and private hire enquiries?

Yes, if you want them. Taxi and private hire enquiries come from drivers, operators and vehicle proprietors dealing with applications, renewals, suspensions, revocations and appeals. Drivers whose licence has been suspended are often under real financial pressure and want help quickly. You can switch taxi work on or off separately from premises work.
Do you send enquiries about temporary event notices?

Event organisers and venues sometimes enquire about one off events, often alongside a wider question about their premises licence. If you want this work, tell us and we will include it in your matching where it fits. Many firms find that a business asking about a single event turns into a longer relationship once it sees how a solicitor can help with its licence more generally.
Volume and areas
How many licensing leads will I receive?

That depends on the licence types, matter types and council areas you choose and the enquiries our campaigns are generating at the time. The minimum is 10 leads a month. Above that, you set the number your team can handle and we match to it. We will give you an honest view on your call, but we cannot promise a fixed number.
Can I choose particular councils?

Yes. Each lead includes the council area, and you can choose particular councils, regions or the whole of England and Wales. Some firms prefer councils whose committees they know well. Others work nationally for multi site operators. Narrower coverage usually means fewer matches, which we will talk through on your call.
Can I set a monthly cap?

Yes. You set the number of leads you want each month, as long as it is at least the minimum of 10. When you reach your cap, we stop matching enquiries to you until the next month. You can change your cap whenever your capacity changes, so you never receive more enquiries than your team can call back promptly.
Can I pause my leads?

Yes. If your team is in a busy run of hearings, someone is on leave or you are changing systems, tell us and we will pause matching until you are ready. Pausing does not end your partner agreement. When you want to restart, let us know and matching begins again as new enquiries come in.
Can leads go to different people in my team?

Yes. We can route by licence type or area, so taxi matters go to one fee earner and premises work to another. We can also send everything to a shared intake inbox or your CRM, where you assign each lead yourself. We set up whatever suits the way your licensing team works.
Do you send enquiries from Scotland?

No. Licensing enquiries come from people and businesses with a matter in England and Wales. Scotland has its own licensing system, so we do not send those enquiries. Within England and Wales, the number of leads you receive depends on the councils, licence types and matter types you choose. Northern Ireland also has its own system.
Can I receive only reviews and hearings?

Yes. Each matter type can be switched on or off, so a firm that concentrates on contested work can ask for reviews, hearings and taxi appeals and leave out routine applications. Contested matters are less common than applications, so a narrow choice usually means fewer leads. We will talk through what is realistic for your areas on your call.
Compliance
Do I need to disclose the referral fee?

Yes. Under the SRA Code of Conduct, you must make sure clients are told in writing about any financial arrangement with an introducer, and that it does not affect your independence or advice. Our consent wording tells every client that we are paid by the firms we introduce them to, and we send that wording with each lead so your client care letter can match it.
Does Leaflegal give licensing advice?

No. Leaflegal is an introduction service, not a law firm. We do not tell clients whether an application will succeed, what conditions to offer or how a committee might decide. We make this clear to every client before they submit. All advice and representation come from your firm. If a client asks us a question about their licence, we tell them the firm will answer it.
Who can receive licensing leads?

SRA regulated firms and CILEx regulated practices authorised for the work, including rights of audience where you appear in the magistrates' court on appeal. You remain responsible for your own conflict checks, client identification and fee arrangements. You must tell us if your authorisation changes, so we can update or pause your matching.
What about conflicts with councils or other venues?

Run your normal conflict checks before taking on a matter. The business name and council area in each lead help you do that before the first call. If you find a conflict, for example because you act for a nearby venue in a related matter or for the licensing authority itself, do not act and let us know, and we will treat the lead as your agreement sets out.
How is client consent recorded?

Each client ticks one box confirming they have read our terms and privacy policy and understand that Leaflegal is an introduction service, and a second box agreeing to their details being shared with one firm that may contact them by phone, email or text. We record the exact wording and the time, and that record arrives with the lead.
How is sensitive data handled?

Reviews and taxi matters can involve allegations of offences or criminal records, which are treated as criminal offence data. We keep questions to the minimum needed for first contact and never share matter details with advertising platforms. Leaflegal, a trading name of Vertical Brands Ltd, is the controller for data collected on our forms, and once a lead is delivered you are controller of your copy.
Pricing and terms
How much does a licensing lead cost?

There is no published price list. You pay per lead at a price agreed with you before you start, based on the licence types, matter types and areas you choose and the volume you want. We put a proposal together after your onboarding call, so you know the cost of every lead before the first one is delivered.
Is there a written agreement?

Yes. Your partner agreement covers pricing, billing, volumes, delivery and the rules on invalid leads, and it is in place before your first lead. Both sides know from the start what is charged, how leads are counted and how any problem with a lead is handled. We go through it with you and answer any questions before you sign.
What counts as an invalid lead?

Your partner agreement sets this out. It usually covers things like wrong contact details or an enquiry outside your agreed criteria. If you think a lead is invalid, tell us within the review period in your agreement and we will deal with it as the agreement says. A client deciding not to instruct does not by itself make a lead invalid.
What if the client only needs a quick question answered?

Some clients start with a narrow question, such as how a transfer works or whether a minor variation might be possible. A lead is an introduction rather than a guaranteed instruction, and how you charge for initial advice is a matter for your firm. Many firms find that a helpful first conversation leads to paid work, either now or later.
Getting started
How do I become a partner firm?

Apply to become a partner firm and book a 30 minute call with our team. We go through the licensing work you handle, the councils you cover, your advocates and your volume. Then we agree your criteria and price, show you a sample lead and put your partner agreement in place before any leads are sent.
Can I see a sample licensing lead?

Yes. On your call we show you a sample licensing lead with every field, the format it arrives in and the consent record. You can see how the licence type, matter type, dates, council area and business name are presented, so you know exactly what your team would receive before you decide.
Is there a portal or login?

No. There is no platform to learn. Leads arrive by email, to a shared intake inbox, or straight into your CRM or case management system using a lead email address or a webhook. Your team works them in the systems they already use, which suits fee earners who spend much of their time at hearings.
What should we set up before our first lead?

Decide who calls new licensing leads and how quickly, especially reviews and taxi suspensions. Route leads to a shared inbox or CRM so someone can always pick them up. Prepare clear fixed fees for common applications and an estimate structure for hearings, and check that your client care letter covers the referral arrangement.
Can we change our criteria later?

Yes. Your matching is not fixed. If you start covering new councils, add a fee earner with taxi experience or decide you want more review work and fewer personal licence enquiries, tell us and we update your criteria. Feedback on which leads instruct and which do not helps us send you more of the licensing work that fits your team.
